problem.title: Product demand cannot reach pages hidden by catalogue complexity
problem.body: Algerian e-commerce sites often spread product discovery across categories, filters, variants, and changing stock. When those routes compete, disappear from internal links, or omit practical purchase information, search engines and local shoppers receive an incomplete view of the catalogue.

method.title: Turn the catalogue into clear search and buying paths
method.intro: The method joins Algerian product demand, crawlable category architecture, and content priorities around how local shoppers compare products and decide what to do next.

steps.title: Map Algerian product demand
steps.body: Group Algerian search themes by product, category, attribute, and buying intent so each useful destination has a defined role in the catalogue.

steps.title: Repair catalogue crawl paths
steps.body: Review Algerian e-commerce navigation, filters, pagination, canonicals, and internal links, using automated checks to surface patterns for direct technical review.

steps.title: Prioritise category content
steps.body: Plan Algerian category and product guidance around genuine selection questions, stock context, delivery coverage, and cash-on-delivery information where it affects the purchase decision.

steps.title: Verify discovery through change
steps.body: Sequence Algerian catalogue fixes by impact and dependency, then verify crawl access, indexation signals, and content placement after templates or inventory states change.

outcome.title: A catalogue that supports discovery before the order decision
outcome.body: Algerian e-commerce teams receive a practical sequence for strengthening category access, reducing competing routes, and publishing the content shoppers need before choosing a product or placing an order.
